messages:
maya: Heads up — we just got a customer escalation: p95/p99 API latencies jumped ~3x for their embed-heavy flows after the node pool CUDA/drivers update at 03:12 UTC. Customer: acme-ai. They included a short trace and timestamps.
trent: copying logs now. any indication it's request size or model-specific?
maya: initial look — spread across multiple models, but higher seq-length requests show worst tail. Not purely application-level.
joan: are these nodes on the cuda13 driver rollout? I think eu-west-2 batch got the update last night.
trent: yes, pool-gpu-3 was on the staged cuda13 drivers. I see a cluster-level spike correlated with the deploy window.
samir: can we repro locally by running a stress harness that mimics their prefix cache + long sequences? I can spin up a node with the same driver.
maya: please repro but also validate host kernel + nvme IO during runs. past regressions were storage contention.
samir: repro steps I'm running:
```
./tools/embed-bench --model rtx-13b --seq 2048 --concurrency 8 --duration 10m --prefix-cache on
```
will attach perf hist when done.
trent: meanwhile, mitigation ideas: 1) move acme-ai traffic to a non-updated pool (pool-gpu-1) 2) reduce batching/turn off large-batch aggregator for that tenant 3) disable preemption/power capping on effected hosts 4) rollback driver if repro confirmed.
maya: moving traffic now to pool-gpu-1 via routing rule. @opsbot please confirm route change.
opsbot: Routing change queued: acme-ai -> pool-gpu-1. Estimated cutover ~40s. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Customer notified: we are investigating and temporarily routing traffic to a different pool. ETA 30m for more details.
samir: repro run results: p99 jumps from ~280ms to ~1.1s on cuda13 node under our harness. Firetrace shows increased NVMe service time and CPU interrupts ~2x during token flush. Attaching synthetic perf summary: nvme_avg_io_ms: 0.6 -> 2.1.
joan: that smells like host kernel->driver interaction. Which kernel version are those hosts on?
trent: hosts are on 6.6.x for the updated pool; fallback pool is 5.15.x. We saw earlier driver ABI shifts with cuda13 and 6.6 combos.
maya: can we try toggling NVMe scheduler or increasing queue depth on a canary to see if latency drops? e.g. echo none > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler or adjust nr_requests?
samir: on a canary I switched scheduler to none and raised queue_depth; perf improved p99 ~1.1s -> 700ms but still worse than baseline. So storage helps but doesn't fully recover.
joan: sounds multi-factor: driver+kernel interaction amplifies NVMe latency which inflates GPU io stall path.
trent: short term: keep traffic on fallback pool for affected customers and throttle long-seq requests via rate limit or reduce concurrency for them. Ops, can we set a per-tenant concurrency cap?
maya: working on a per-tenant limiter for acme-ai: set concurrency=4, max_seq=1024 for 2 hours.
opsbot: Per-tenant rule applied: concurrency=4, max_seq=1024 for tenant acme-ai.
samir: next steps for infra: 1) collect full perf traces (fio, iostat, softirq) on updated pool hosts 2) engage driver vendor if kernel-driver mismatch reproduces 3) schedule driver rollback if vendor fix not immediate 4) update rollout gating to include nvme p99 metrics.
joan: also add a canary that uses real-world request shapes, not just microbench. That would've caught this.
maya: I'll file an incident follow-up with timeline, customer impact, mitigations, and action items (rollback plan + rollout gating). Assigning owners: samir (repro & perf traces), trent (routing + rollback), joan (driver vendor + kernel coordination), me (customer comms + postmortem).
trent: rolling snapshot of the impacted hosts now and saving kernel logs.
samir: attaching short perf excerpt here (summarized):
- baseline (5.15): nvme_avg_ms 0.6, p99_io 4.2ms, app p99 280ms
- updated (6.6 + cuda13): nvme_avg_ms 2.1, p99_io 28ms, app p99 1.1s
maya: thanks. keep comms in this thread. I'll update the customer once we have rollback decision.
joan: +1 on making nvme p99 a rollout gating metric. Also propose an automated rollback trigger if app p99 > 2x baseline for 15m.
trent: noted. if rollback goes ahead, coordinate maintenance window.
maya: end-of-thread summary: routing moved, tenant throttle applied, repro confirmed on cuda13+6.6, storage contributes, next: vendor engagement or rollback, add gating.
__notes: Slack thread: short messages, @mentions and bot confirmations included. No title field per agents.md.
